groups.sentence: Administrators update or clarify honor codes and conduct policies to cover generative AI.
Instructors state in their syllabus or remind students that unauthorized AI use is academic misconduct.
Students do not use AI to fabricate information, evade detection, conceal use, or circumvent learning goals.
Students do not use unauthorized AI during exams or assessments.
Unauthorized or improper AI use is academic misconduct or an academic integrity violation.
AI violations are handled through existing academic integrity and conduct processes, with possible disciplinary action.
Students do not use AI tools without authorization or in ways that violate instructor or university rules.
Presenting AI-generated or uncited AI content as one's own work is plagiarism.
Students do not present AI-generated content as their own work or use it without attribution or citation.
Any use of generative AI in the course is a violation.
Using unauthorized AI counts as cheating or unauthorized assistance.
Instructors enforce academic integrity policies and treat unauthorized AI use like other violations when misuse is found.
Students follow the university's honor code and academic integrity rules when using AI.
Using AI is not inherently misconduct; concerns arise when use breaks course expectations.
